# Thereabouts data dictionary

Thereabouts is an offline geocoder. A Parquet dataset holds the open data; binary packs built from it answer lookups through the Python, Node and command-line clients and the MCP server. This dictionary is generated from the schema file, the client code and the Rust core, so it describes exactly the tables and tools of the build that produced it.

## Pack families

Each family is an installable pack that answers one kind of question. Forward families use the `core` pack, when installed, for city and timezone detail.

### `core`

Reverse geocoding and city names. A latitude and longitude, or an H3 cell, gives country, subdivision, city and timezone; a town or city name gives the matching cities.

- Tools: `reverse`, `h3`, `geocode`
- Inputs: Coordinates in WGS84 degrees; an H3 cell of resolution 0 to 8 as 15 hexadecimal characters; a city name of at most 128 normalized characters.
- Built from tables: `cells`, `places`, `canonical_cities`, `place_to_city`, `names`, `countries`, `subdivisions`, `timezone_cells`, `zone_tables`
- Notes: Every other family reads the core pack for city and timezone detail when it is installed. geocode finds towns and cities by canonical, English or alternate name (the names table), never street addresses.

### `postal`

Postal code to place.

- Tools: `postal`
- Inputs: A code and the country it belongs to. Codes repeat across countries, so the country is required. Spaces are ignored; hyphens and leading zeros are kept.
- Built from tables: `postal_codes`, `places`, `canonical_cities`, `place_to_city`, `countries`, `subdivisions`
- Notes: One code can name several places; the result is then ambiguous with ranked candidates.

### `airports`

Airport code to airport.

- Tools: `airport`
- Inputs: A code and an optional scheme (iata, icao, gps, local or ident). Without a scheme, IATA then ICAO are searched. The local scheme needs a country.
- Built from tables: `airports`, `places`, `canonical_cities`, `place_to_city`, `countries`, `subdivisions`
- Notes: Ambiguous codes return ranked candidates; a country narrows them.

### `locode`

UN/LOCODE to trade or transport location (port, airport, rail or road terminal).

- Tools: `locode`
- Inputs: The five-character code (two country letters and three letters or digits), or three characters plus a country.
- Built from tables: `trade_locations`, `places`, `canonical_cities`, `place_to_city`, `countries`, `subdivisions`
- Notes: Conflicting or malformed country hints are invalid input.

### `phone`

International telephone number to the longest published calling prefix and its country.

- Tools: `phone`
- Inputs: A number in E.164 form with a leading plus and 1 to 15 digits; spaces, hyphens and parentheses after the plus are ignored.
- Built from tables: `phone_prefixes`, `phone_metadata`, `places`, `canonical_cities`, `place_to_city`, `countries`, `subdivisions`
- Notes: This is prefix lookup, not subscriber validation. Shared calling codes such as +1 return one candidate per country.

### `ip`

IPv4 or IPv6 address to the published geolocation interval that contains it.

- Tools: `ip`
- Inputs: A bare address literal; ports, CIDR suffixes and IPv6 zones are invalid.
- Built from tables: `ip_ranges`, `places`, `canonical_cities`, `place_to_city`, `countries`, `subdivisions`
- Notes: The point is the provider's location for the interval, usually a city centre, not the device.

### `plates`

Vehicle registration plate text to the countries, and sometimes the region, whose recorded formats it fits.

- Tools: `plate`
- Inputs: Plate text and an optional country and series.
- Built from tables: `plate_formats`, `plate_codes`, `plate_policy`, `plate_priors`, `places`, `canonical_cities`, `place_to_city`, `countries`, `subdivisions`
- Notes: Format evidence, not a vehicle registry. Without a country the result is usually ambiguous across countries.

## Tools

Every tool is read-only, never installs data and never uses the network. Lookup tools return the result object described below.

### `reverse`

Find the country, subdivision, city and timezone at a latitude and longitude.

Needs the core pack. status is matched when stored land covers the point
and not_found otherwise: open water, land outside the installed coverage,
or unassigned land. match says how the city was chosen: contained (inside
a boundary), nearest (nearest settlement within the distant threshold) or
nearest_distant (farther; treat the city as approximate), and
distance_band bounds that distance in kilometres. point and cell describe
the resolution 8 H3 cell that holds the input, not the input itself. With
evidence, a miss explains itself (no_land, outside_coverage, unassigned)
and a match shows the city_method that chose the city.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lat` | number | yes |  | Latitude in degrees, -90 to 90 |
| `lon` | number | yes |  | Longitude in degrees, -180 to 180 |
| `evidence` | boolean | no | `false` | Add the audit evidence: why the answer or the miss, and sources |

### `h3`

Find the stored ancestor of an H3 cell at resolution zero to eight.

Needs the core pack. Like reverse, from a cell instead of a point.
Cells of resolution 3 to 8 search themselves and their stored ancestors;
resolutions 0 to 2 have no stored ancestor and return not_found. A
resolution above 8 or a malformed cell is invalid_input.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cell` | string | yes |  | H3 cell as 15 hexadecimal characters, resolution 0 to 8 |
| `evidence` | boolean | no | `false` | Add the audit evidence: why the answer or the miss, and sources |

### `geocode`

Finds towns and cities by name. Street addresses are not supported.

Needs the core pack. status is matched for one city and ambiguous when
several share the name: candidates are ranked by population and the
flat fields keep only what every candidate shares. Pass country or
subdivision to narrow them, or prefer="population" to take the largest.
match is exact, alternate_name (a published English or other name) or
fuzzy (typo tolerant; check the returned name). A street address is
unsupported_granularity.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | string | yes |  | City or town name, not an address |
| `country` | string or null | no | `null` | Two-letter country code; a hard filter |
| `subdivision` | string or null | no | `null` | Subdivision code such as US-IL; a hard filter |
| `limit` | integer | no | `5` | Most candidates to return, 1 to 100 |
| `prefer` | string or null | no | `null` | "population" picks the most populous of several cities |
| `evidence` | boolean | no | `false` | Add the audit evidence: why the answer or the miss, and sources |

### `postal`

Find a postal code in the required source country.

Needs the postal pack. Spaces are ignored; hyphens and leading zeros are
kept. A code that names several places is ambiguous: candidates are
ranked by population. A malformed country, such as a country name
instead of its two-letter code, is invalid_input.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | string | yes |  | The code to look up; leading zeros matter |
| `country` | string | yes |  | Two-letter country code of the postal system |
| `evidence` | boolean | no | `false` | Add the audit evidence: why the answer or the miss, and sources |

### `airport`

Find an airport by IATA/ICAO or a specified code scheme.

Needs the airports pack. The point is the airport's own point and the
city is the canonical city around it, which can differ from the name in
the airport's title. The local scheme needs a country; an unknown scheme
is invalid_input. A code shared by several airports is ambiguous.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | string | yes |  | The code to look up; leading zeros matter |
| `scheme` | string or null | no | `null` | iata, icao, gps, local or ident; omit for IATA then ICAO |
| `country` | string or null | no | `null` | Two-letter country code; narrows ambiguous codes |
| `evidence` | boolean | no | `false` | Add the audit evidence: why the answer or the miss, and sources |

### `locode`

Find a trade location by its five-character LOCODE.

Needs the locode pack. Evidence carries the function flags, status and
remarks. A malformed code or a conflicting country is invalid_input; an
unknown code is not_found.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | string | yes |  | UN/LOCODE, e.g. BEANR, or three characters with country |
| `country` | string or null | no | `null` | Two-letter country code when the code has three characters |
| `evidence` | boolean | no | `false` | Add the audit evidence: why the answer or the miss, and sources |

### `phone`

Find the longest published prefix of an international E.164 number.

Needs the phone pack. This is prefix lookup, not subscriber validation.
A calling code shared by several countries, such as +1, can be
ambiguous with one candidate per country unless country narrows it. A
number without the leading plus is invalid_input.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `number` | string | yes |  | E.164 number with a leading plus and 1 to 15 digits |
| `country` | string or null | no | `null` | Two-letter country code; narrows a shared calling code |
| `evidence` | boolean | no | `false` | Add the audit evidence: why the answer or the miss, and sources |

### `ip`

Find published context for an IPv4 or IPv6 literal.

Needs the ip pack. The answer is the geolocation provider's location for
the interval that contains the address, usually a city centre; it is not
the location of the device. An address outside the published intervals, for
example a loopback address, is not_found.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | string | yes |  | IPv4 or IPv6 address literal, without port or mask |
| `evidence` | boolean | no | `false` | Add the audit evidence: why the answer or the miss, and sources |

### `plate`

Find recorded registration formats, preserving country ambiguity.

Needs the plates pack. The result is format evidence, not a vehicle
registry. Without a country, plates usually fit formats of several
countries and the result is ambiguous with candidates ranked by evidence
(rank_basis). With a country the answer is that country, and evidence
explains how much geography the code supports.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | string | yes |  | Vehicle registration plate text |
| `country` | string or null | no | `null` | Two-letter country context; stays exact when given |
| `series` | string or null | no | `null` | Series or subdivision context for series-based plates |
| `evidence` | boolean | no | `false` | Add the audit evidence: why the answer or the miss, and sources |

### `describe`

Describe the open Parquet dataset behind the answers.

Without a table, lists every table with its purpose, grain, key and
number of columns. With a table, returns its columns (type, nullability,
units, meaning), primary key, joins to other tables, and the enumerated
values of coded columns. Use it before writing SQL over the dataset.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `table` | string or null | no | `null` | Dataset table name; omit to list every table |

## Resources

- `thereabouts://dictionary` (application/json): Dataset tables, columns, joins and enumerations, pack families, tools and result fields. From the installed core pack when it ships one.
- `thereabouts://dictionary/markdown` (text/markdown): The same dictionary as readable Markdown.

## Result

Every lookup tool returns one result object. `evidence` appears only when requested and `hint` only when the input needs correction.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | string (values: `status`) | Typed outcome; misses and invalid query values are ordinary results |
| `kind` | string (values: `kind`) | Domain of the answer; reverse uses cell |
| `match` | string or null (values: `match`) | Published spatial method, absent for misses and invalid inputs |
| `country` | Country or null | Matched country or the country shared by every ambiguous candidate |
| `state` | State or null | Flat subdivision context, using indexed metadata |
| `city` | City or null | Final published canonical city or rural settlement |
| `timezone` | string or null | Single country-valid zone; unresolved overlap stays in evidence |
| `point` | Point or null | Representative query-cell centre for reverse lookups |
| `cell` | string or null | Canonical query H3 cell; coarse inputs retain their own resolution |
| `distance_band` | DistanceBand or null | Published nearest-policy interval, absent for contained results |
| `candidates` | array of Result | Ranked forward candidates; reverse always leaves this empty |
| `rank_basis` | string or null (values: `rank_basis`) | Forward ranking rule, absent for reverse lookups |
| `evidence` | Evidence or null | Opt-in audit fields, omitted from JSON when not requested |
| `hint` | string or null | Actionable input guidance, emitted only when a query needs correction |

### `Country`

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | string | Published two-letter country code |
| `code3` | string or null | Published alpha-3 code, or null when unavailable |
| `name` | string | Country display name from the place catalogue |

### `State`

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | string or null | Published subdivision code, falling back to the place code only if no row exists |
| `name` | string | Subdivision table name, falling back only when the row is absent |

### `City`

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Stable canonical city or final rural-settlement identity |
| `name` | string | Published canonical display name; never reconstructed by the client |
| `name_en` | string or null | English name when the dataset supplies one |
| `kind` | string | Published settlement class such as city, town or village |
| `population` | integer or null | Published population, with unknown zero represented as null |
| `point` | Point or null | Published catalogue anchor, independent of the query cell centre |

### `Point`

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lat` | number | Latitude in geographic degrees |
| `lon` | number | Longitude in geographic degrees |

### `DistanceBand`

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `greater_than_km` | number | Exclusive lower policy bound in kilometres |
| `at_most_km` | number | Inclusive upper policy bound in kilometres |

### `Evidence`

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stored_cell` | string or null | Stored pack ancestor, possibly split by a timezone boundary |
| `country_id` | string or null | Country catalogue identity behind the spatial label |
| `state_id` | string or null | Subdivision catalogue identity behind the spatial label |
| `city_id` | string or null | Final city or settlement identity behind the spatial label |
| `city_method` | string or null (values: `cells.city_method`) | Original golden assignment method, when a city is assigned |
| `land_method` | string or null (values: `cells.land_method`) | Published land or offshore eligibility marker |
| `reason` | string or null (values: `evidence.reason`) | Detailed matched or not-found reason without changing public status |
| `timezones` | array of string | Unresolved zone survivors after country narrowing; empty for a unique zone |
| `source_ids` | array of objects or null | Source identifiers published in the city catalogue evidence |

### `status`

- `matched`: Published geography or one resolved place
- `ambiguous`: Several ranked places; flat fields retain only candidate consensus
- `not_found`: No stored answer for the query
- `invalid_input`: The query cannot be interpreted in this domain
- `unsupported_granularity`: The input requests detail finer than the dataset supports

### `kind`

- `city`: A canonical city or rural settlement
- `cell`: A spatial cell, including country-only reverse context
- `postal`: A postal code with a published anchor
- `airport`: An airport identified by a supported code
- `trade_location`: A port or other transport location
- `ip_range`: A published IP address interval
- `phone_prefix`: A published calling-code or telephone prefix
- `plate`: A vehicle registration format or series

### `match`

- `exact`: An exact normalized identifier or primary name
- `alternate_name`: A published English or alternate name
- `fuzzy`: A fuzzy name-index match
- `contained`: The dataset publishes polygon or area containment
- `nearest`: The published nearest-distance band below the distant threshold
- `nearest_distant`: The published nearest-distance band above the distant threshold

### `evidence.reason`

- `matched` (reverse, h3): A stored cell supplied the geography
- `unassigned` (reverse, h3): A stored cell exists but has no country, subdivision or city; the status is not_found
- `no_land` (reverse, h3): The cell's block is in the pack but no land is stored at this resolution 8 cell, as in open water. In a subset pack it means no admitted land row, not a global ocean assertion
- `outside_coverage` (reverse, h3): The cell's block is not in the pack, so the point is outside the pack's coverage
- `no_stored_ancestor` (reverse, h3): A coarse H3 query (resolution 0 to 7) has no stored cell at or above it
- `name_exact` (geocode): The normalized query equals a canonical or alternate city name
- `name_prefix` (geocode): No exact name; the query is the start of a city name
- `name_trigram` (geocode): No exact or prefix name; an approximate (fuzzy) name match
- `exact_code` (postal, airport, locode, phone, ip): The normalized code or address equals an indexed key or falls in an indexed interval
- `country_from_key` (postal): The postal observation has no linked geography, so its country comes from the country in the lookup key; no subdivision or city is inferred
- `plate_country_inferred` (plate): No country was supplied; this candidate country was inferred from format evidence and no finer geography is returned
- `empty_or_too_long_input` (plate): The plate text was empty after normalization or longer than the policy maximum
- `known_registration_code` (plate): The code is a known registration code for the place or places listed in the evidence
- `known_state_code_no_finer_verified_unit` (plate): The code identifies a state-level registration unit and no finer verified unit
- `unknown_code_or_unverified_temporal_scope` (plate): The format fits, but the code is not a known registration code or its dates are unverified, so only the country is returned
- `no_matching_format` (plate): No recorded plate format of the country matches the text
- `subdivision_series_context_required` (plate): The country issues plates by subdivision series; pass series to narrow the geography
- `non_geographic_or_ambiguous_series` (plate): A matching format carries no geographic code or is ambiguous, so no geography is returned

### `rank_basis`

- `population` (geocode, postal, airport, locode, phone, ip): Candidates are ordered by city population, largest first, with a stable order for ties
- `plate_evidence` (plate): Candidate countries are ordered by format evidence and a vehicle-registration prior
- `plate_evidence_without_vehicle_prior` (plate): Candidate countries are ordered by format evidence alone because the pack has no vehicle prior

### Error codes

- `closed_geocoder`: An operation was attempted after closing a geocoder
- `corrupt_pack`: A pack's checksum, record, or inventory failed validation
- `data_not_installed`: No core pack is installed in the selected store
- `geocoder_error`: Base class for offline geocoder failures
- `incompatible_data`: The selected pack requires a different reader or family
- `internal_error`: A library invariant failed, such as a poisoned lock; please report it
- `invalid_input`: A value could not be encoded or looked up; the pack itself is fine
- `pack_not_found`: An explicitly selected pack directory does not exist
- `resource_limit`: The process ran out of file descriptors; raise the open-file limit
- `writer_error`: A staging or output operation failed during dataset export
- `writer_input_error`: Dataset input, options or staging state prevents export

## Dataset tables

Plain Parquet files, one directory per table. Directory labels (`country=XX`, `group=...`) route files and are not stored columns; DuckDB and PyArrow add them as columns unless Hive partitioning is off. Only the keys listed are guaranteed unique, and assembly refuses a release that repeats one. Observation tables are keyed by `source` and `source_id`, one row per source record, so a code or name can repeat across rows.

| Table | Grain | Key | Feeds packs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`airports`](#airports) | One row per airport record in the pinned OurAirports file; duplicate observations are retained. | `source`, `source_id` | `airports` |
| [`blocks`](#blocks) | One row per covered resolution 3 block, including blocks that store no cells. A block absent from this table is outside the coverage of this export. | `block` | none |
| [`canonical_cities`](#canonical_cities) | One row per canonical city or town; city_id is the place identifier of its anchor. | `city_id` | `core`, `postal`, `airports`, `locode`, `phone`, `ip`, `plates` |
| [`cells`](#cells) | One row per stored H3 cell: a resolution 8 cell, or a coarser ancestor (resolution 3 to 7) that stands for all its resolution 8 descendants when they share one label. | `h3_uint64` | `core` |
| [`countries`](#countries) | One row per country or territory code in the pinned sources. | `country_code` | `core`, `postal`, `airports`, `locode`, `phone`, `ip`, `plates` |
| [`ip_ranges`](#ip_ranges) | One row per published IP interval, from ip_start to ip_end inclusive. | `source`, `source_id` | `ip` |
| [`names`](#names) | One row per canonical city and distinct name. Names that fold to the same text, or to the city's canonical or English name, are kept once. | `city_id`, `name` | `core` |
| [`phone_metadata`](#phone_metadata) | One row per libphonenumber territory, including the non-geographic territory 001. | `source`, `source_id` | `phone` |
| [`phone_prefixes`](#phone_prefixes) | One row per prefix description in one language file, so a prefix repeats once per language. | `source`, `source_id` | `phone` |
| [`place_to_city`](#place_to_city) | One row per place; every places row has exactly one mapping row. | `place_id` | `core`, `postal`, `airports`, `locode`, `phone`, `ip`, `plates` |
| [`places`](#places) | One row per reconciled place. | `place_id` | `core`, `postal`, `airports`, `locode`, `phone`, `ip`, `plates` |
| [`plate_codes`](#plate_codes) | One row per source assertion of a code; a code repeats across sources, series and validity periods. | none | `plates` |
| [`plate_formats`](#plate_formats) | One row per source rule; a country has one row per modeled series and source. | none | `plates` |
| [`plate_policy`](#plate_policy) | Exactly one row. | none | `plates` |
| [`plate_priors`](#plate_priors) | One row per country with a published count. | `country_code` | `plates` |
| [`postal_codes`](#postal_codes) | One row per postal-code observation; a code can repeat for different place names or variants. | `source`, `source_id` | `postal` |
| [`subdivisions`](#subdivisions) | One row per GeoNames first-level division code. | `code` | `core`, `postal`, `airports`, `locode`, `phone`, `ip`, `plates` |
| [`timezone_cells`](#timezone_cells) | One row per timezone and H3 cell; a cell in overlapping zones has several rows, and cells are stored at resolutions 0 to 8. | `source`, `source_id` | `core` |
| [`trade_locations`](#trade_locations) | One row per UN/LOCODE entry in the pinned files; source_id names its file and row, and a location code can repeat across entries. | `source`, `source_id` | `locode` |
| [`zone_tables`](#zone_tables) | One row per entry of an IANA zone table; a timezone can appear in several tables. | `source`, `source_id` | `core` |

### `airports`

Airports and airfields from OurAirports, placed on the H3 grid and joined to the cell geography at their coordinates.

- Grain: One row per airport record in the pinned OurAirports file; duplicate observations are retained.
- Primary key: `source`, `source_id`
- Feeds packs: `airports`

Joins:

- `airports.country_id` → `places.place_id`: The country place of the cell the point falls in; null when the row is unlocated or unassigned
- `airports.state_id` → `places.place_id`: The first-level subdivision place of that cell; null when none is assigned
- `airports.city_id` → `places.place_id`: The selected settlement of that cell, a canonical city or a standalone rural settlement; null when none is assigned

| Column | Type | Nullable | Units | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | `string` | yes in Arrow; no for the logical key |  | Configured upstream source name |
| `source_id` | `string` | yes in Arrow; no for the logical key |  | Identifier of the original observation within its source |
| `ident` | `string` | yes |  | OurAirports airport identifier |
| `iata_code` | `string` | yes |  | IATA airport code, where available |
| `icao_code` | `string` | yes |  | ICAO airport code, where available |
| `gps_code` | `string` | yes |  | Source GPS airport code |
| `local_code` | `string` | yes |  | Local airport code |
| `type` | `string` | yes |  | Source-specific entity classification |
| `name` | `string` | yes |  | Preferred display name |
| `municipality` | `string` | yes |  | Source municipality text |
| `country_code` | `string` | yes |  | Source or reconciled ISO-like two-letter country code |
| `region_code` | `string` | yes |  | Source region or subdivision code |
| `latitude` | `double` | yes | degrees north | WGS84 latitude; positive north |
| `longitude` | `double` | yes | degrees east | WGS84 longitude; positive east |
| `h3` | `string` | yes |  | Lowercase hexadecimal H3 cell index, without 0x |
| `h3_uint64` | `uint64` | yes |  | Same H3 index as an unsigned 64-bit integer |
| `h3_resolution` | `uint8` | yes | H3 level | Resolution of this stored H3 index |
| `source_release` | `string` | yes |  | Pinned upstream release or inventory identifier |
| `license` | `string` | yes |  | Upstream licence identifier |
| `provenance` | `string` | yes |  | JSON source evidence and transformation provenance |
| `country_id` | `string` | yes |  | Reconciled country place identifier |
| `state_id` | `string` | yes |  | Reconciled first-level subdivision place identifier |
| `city_id` | `string` | yes |  | Selected settlement place ID, including standalone rural settlements; null if unassigned |
| `cell_country_code` | `string` | yes |  | Country code assigned by the geographic cell join |
| `cell_status` | `string` | yes |  | Cell join status: matched, unassigned, ineligible, pending or unlocated |
| `country_disagrees` | `bool` | yes |  | Whether source and cell country codes disagree; null if not comparable |

Enumerated columns:

- `cell_status`
  - `matched`: The point's cell is stored and has a country assignment
  - `unassigned`: The cell is stored but no country is assigned to it
  - `ineligible`: The cell is outside the stored land and near-shore coverage
  - `pending`: No cell data exists for the point's block in this release, so no decision was made
  - `unlocated`: The row has no coordinates, so there is no cell to join

### `blocks`

The block index of the cells table: every covered resolution 3 H3 block, the cells file and Parquet row group that hold its rows, and how much it stores. A reader can route a coordinate to its rows with this table alone, without manifest.json. Release assembly builds it from the cells it writes.

- Grain: One row per covered resolution 3 block, including blocks that store no cells. A block absent from this table is outside the coverage of this export.
- Primary key: `block`
- Feeds packs: none

| Column | Type | Nullable | Units | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `block` | `string` | no |  | Resolution 3 H3 block in lowercase hexadecimal without 0x; equals cells.block of every row it stores |
| `cell_group` | `string` | no |  | Resolution 1 H3 parent of the block in lowercase hexadecimal; the block's cells file sits in the directory cells/group=<cell_group>/ |
| `path` | `string` | no |  | The cells file that holds the block's rows, relative to the dataset directory; for a block without rows, the file whose manifest entry lists it as empty |
| `row_group` | `int64` | yes |  | Zero-based Parquet row group in path that holds every row of the block; null when the block stores no cells |
| `row_count` | `int64` | no | rows | Cells rows stored for the block; 0 when it stores none, and lookups there then answer that the location is not on land |
| `reference_cells` | `int64` | no | H3 resolution 8 cells | Resolution 8 cells that the block's stored rows stand for once compacted rows are expanded; at most 16,807 |

### `canonical_cities`

The cities and towns that can absorb other settlements, the anchors for urban areas. Reverse lookups can also return standalone villages and other rural settlements, which are in places but not here.

- Grain: One row per canonical city or town; city_id is the place identifier of its anchor.
- Primary key: `city_id`
- Feeds packs: `core`, `postal`, `airports`, `locode`, `phone`, `ip`, `plates`

Joins:

- `canonical_cities.city_id` → `places.place_id`: The anchor place of the canonical city
- `canonical_cities.place_id` → `places.place_id`: The reconciled place of the canonical city; equal to city_id

| Column | Type | Nullable | Units | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `city_id` | `string` | no |  | Canonical city/town anchor ID |
| `place_id` | `string` | no |  | Reconciled place identifier |
| `country_code` | `string` | no |  | Source or reconciled ISO-like two-letter country code |
| `kind` | `string` | no |  | Canonical settlement kind |
| `name` | `string` | no |  | Preferred display name |
| `eligibility` | `string` | no |  | Evidence qualifying this place as a canonical city |
| `name_en` | `string` | yes |  | Preferred name only when its provenance explicitly identifies English |
| `latitude` | `double` | no | degrees north | WGS84 latitude; positive north |
| `longitude` | `double` | no | degrees east | WGS84 longitude; positive east |
| `population` | `int64` | yes | people | Source population estimate, not a current census assertion |
| `source_ids` | `string` | no |  | JSON list of contributing source identifiers |
| `footprint_references` | `string` | no |  | JSON references to source settlement footprints |
| `allocation_rule` | `string` | no |  | Rule used to allocate this canonical settlement |

Enumerated columns:

- `kind`
  - `city`: A city: classified as a city by the source, or with a population of at least 100,000
  - `town`: A town that is not classified as a city and has a smaller population
- `eligibility`
  - `typed town/city and seat or population`: Classified as a town or city by the source, and either a seat feature code or a population at or above the typed minimum
  - `population and active settlement`: Population at or above the policy minimum, and a feature code that the policy does not exclude
  - `national or first-order seat`: A national capital or first-order administrative seat feature code
  - `explicit country policy`: Named by the country's city policy
  - `linked city overrides section code`: A source city classification overrides the section feature code that would exclude it
- `allocation_rule`
  - `bounded`: The city has accepted boundary footprints that own the cells inside them
  - `urban_allocation; optional town_radius`: No boundary: the city receives urban cells by allocation and, when enabled, cells within its town radius

### `cells`

Reverse-geocoding labels for land and the retained near-shore band on the H3 grid: country, subdivision and city, with the evidence behind each. Cells are losslessly compacted, so a row can stand for many resolution 8 cells.

- Grain: One row per stored H3 cell: a resolution 8 cell, or a coarser ancestor (resolution 3 to 7) that stands for all its resolution 8 descendants when they share one label.
- Primary key: `h3_uint64`
- Feeds packs: `core`

Joins:

- `cells.country_id` → `places.place_id`: The country place of the cell; null when no country is assigned
- `cells.state_id` → `places.place_id`: The first-level subdivision place of the cell; null when none is assigned
- `cells.city_id` → `places.place_id`: The selected settlement of the cell, a canonical city or a standalone rural settlement; null when none is assigned
- `cells.block` → `blocks.block`: The block that routes the cell to its file and Parquet row group

| Column | Type | Nullable | Units | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `h3` | `string` | no |  | Lowercase hexadecimal H3 cell index, without 0x |
| `h3_uint64` | `uint64` | no |  | Same H3 index as an unsigned 64-bit integer |
| `h3_resolution` | `uint8` | no | H3 level | Resolution of this stored H3 index |
| `country_id` | `string` | yes |  | Reconciled country place identifier |
| `state_id` | `string` | yes |  | Reconciled first-level subdivision place identifier |
| `city_id` | `string` | yes |  | Selected settlement place ID, including standalone rural settlements; null if unassigned |
| `country_method` | `string` | yes |  | Country assignment evidence: area, or null when absent |
| `state_method` | `string` | yes |  | Subdivision assignment evidence: area, or null when absent |
| `city_method` | `string` | yes |  | Canonical city allocation rule, including distant-nearest classification |
| `land_method` | `string` | yes |  | Land eligibility evidence: land or offshore |
| `block` | `string` | no |  | Resolution 3 H3 parent of the cell (its block) in lowercase hexadecimal without 0x. Each Parquet row group holds one block, so filtering on block reads one row group |

Enumerated columns:

- `country_method`
  - `area`: The cell centre lies inside the country's boundary area
- `state_method`
  - `area`: The cell centre lies inside the subdivision's boundary area
- `city_method`
  - `city_polygon`: Inside an accepted municipal footprint polygon of a canonical city
  - `policy_polygon`: Inside an area that country policy assigns to one city
  - `urban_allocation`: An urban cell outside any footprint, allocated to a canonical city of its urban cluster
  - `town_radius`: A rural cell within a qualifying town's own radius; an optional rule that policy can disable
  - `rural_polygon`: Inside the boundary polygon of a standalone rural settlement
  - `rural_nearest`: No polygon covers the cell; the nearest settlement within the distant threshold
  - `rural_nearest_distant`: The nearest settlement is farther than the distant threshold and within the nearest cutoff; treat the city as approximate
- `land_method`
  - `land`: The cell centre is on land
  - `offshore`: A retained near-shore water cell whose assignment is projected from nearby land

| `intermediate_region_code` | `string` | yes |  | UN intermediate region code |
| `intermediate_region_name` | `string` | yes |  | UN intermediate region name |
| `source_release` | `string` | no |  | Pinned upstream release or inventory identifier |
| `license` | `string` | no |  | Upstream licence identifier |
| `provenance` | `string` | no |  | JSON source evidence and transformation provenance |
| `country_id` | `string` | yes |  | Reconciled country place identifier |
| `place_id` | `string` | yes |  | Uniquely matched reconciled place; null for ambiguous or unmatched observations |
| `link_status` | `string` | yes |  | Identifier link status: matched, ambiguous, unmatched or pending |
| `link_method` | `string` | yes |  | Rule used for the identifier link |
| `place_ids` | `list<element: string>` | yes |  | All candidate place identifiers; ambiguity is preserved |

Enumerated columns:

- `link_status`
  - `matched`: Exactly one candidate place; place_id is set
  - `ambiguous`: Several candidate places; all are in place_ids and place_id is null
  - `unmatched`: No candidate place was found
  - `pending`: The row refers to a country that is expected in the release but was not reconciled in this build
- `link_method`
  - `source country code`: The row's own country code identifies the country
  - `explicit code or administrative crosswalk`: The published subdivision code maps to a place through the code crosswalk
  - `GeoNames administrative identity`: The row's GeoNames identifier identifies the place
  - `exact country-scoped administrative alias`: The normalized name equals a place alias within the same country
  - `source-qualified administrative alias`: A name qualified by its source administrative context equals a place alias
  - `territory fixed-line prefix language`: Candidate countries were narrowed by the territory's fixed-line numbering pattern
  - `no numbering-pattern support; retained source candidates`: No numbering pattern could narrow the candidates, so every source country is kept

### `ip_ranges`

IPv4 and IPv6 geolocation intervals from DB-IP City Lite, each with a published point joined to the cell geography. The ip pack writer rejects overlapping intervals.

- Grain: One row per published IP interval, from ip_start to ip_end inclusive.

### `names`

Alternate names of canonical cities: every name the core pack's forward geocoder matches for a city beyond its canonical and English names in canonical_cities. Names come from GeoNames alternate names, GeoNames feature and ASCII names, and Overture division names of the city's own place or a declared identity alias, filtered by config/policies/names.yaml.

- Grain: One row per canonical city and distinct name. Names that fold to the same text, or to the city's canonical or English name, are kept once.

- Feeds packs: `core`

- `names.city_id` → `canonical_cities.city_id`: The canonical city the name finds

### `place_to_city`

The reviewed mapping from every place to the city or standalone settlement that represents it. Use it to roll places up to canonical cities.

- Grain: One row per place; every places row has exactly one mapping row.
- Primary key: `place_id`
- Feeds packs: `core`, `postal`, `airports`, `locode`, `phone`, `ip`, `plates`

Joins:

- `place_to_city.place_id` → `places.place_id`: The mapped place
- `place_to_city.city_id` → `places.place_id`: The representing city or settlement; null for non-settlements

| Column | Type | Nullable | Units | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `place_id` | `string` | no |  | Reconciled place identifier |
| `city_id` | `string` | yes |  | Selected settlement place ID, including standalone rural settlements; null if unassigned |
| `method` | `string` | no |  | Mapping rule: self, spatial_absorption, policy_part, identity_alias or non_settlement |
| `evidence` | `string` | yes |  | JSON evidence supporting the allocation |

Enumerated columns:

- `method`
  - `self`: The place is its own city: a canonical city, or a settlement that no city absorbs
  - `spatial_absorption`: The settlement lies inside a canonical city's extent and maps to that city
  - `policy_part`: Country policy names the place as a part of a city and maps it there
  - `identity_alias`: Country policy declares the place another identity of the same city
  - `non_settlement`: A country, state or district: not a settlement, so city_id is null

### `places`

  - `insufficient settlement evidence`: A locality without enough settlement evidence to be a city or town
  - `administrative container of a larger linked settlement`: A district that contains a much larger linked settlement
- `role`
  - `country`: A country
  - `state`: A first-level subdivision
  - `city`: A canonical city
  - `town`: A canonical town
  - `settlement`: A settlement that is not a canonical city or town
  - `district`: An administrative district or a locality without settlement evidence
- `normalization_method`
  - `self`: The place is its own city: a canonical city, or a settlement that no city absorbs
  - `spatial_absorption`: The settlement lies inside a canonical city's extent and maps to that city
  - `policy_part`: Country policy names the place as a part of a city and maps it there
  - `identity_alias`: Country policy declares the place another identity of the same city
  - `non_settlement`: A country, state or district: not a settlement, so city_id is null
- `settlement_kind`
  - `country`: A country
  - `state`: A first-level subdivision
  - `district`: An administrative district
  - `city`: A canonical city, or a standalone settlement the source classifies as a city
  - `town`: A canonical town, or a standalone settlement the source classifies as a town
  - `city_part`: A place that the mapping absorbs into another city
  - `village`: A standalone settlement classified as a village
  - `hamlet`: A standalone settlement classified as a hamlet
  - `settlement`: A standalone settlement without a source class

### `plate_codes`

Registration-code assertions: a code printed on vehicle plates and the registration unit or entity it names, from pinned national pages, Wikipedia revisions and Wikidata. Every row keeps its source URL and licence.

- Grain: One row per source assertion of a code; a code repeats across sources, series and validity periods.
- Primary key: none
- Feeds packs: `plates`

Joins:

- `plate_codes.country_code` → `countries.country_code`: The country or territory issuing the plates

| Column | Type | Nullable | Units | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `country_code` | `string` | no |  | ISO-like two-letter code of the issuing country or territory |
| `code` | `string` | no |  | The code as the source spells it, with leading zeros and native script |
| `name_en` | `string` | yes |  | English label of the registration unit, as published |
| `name_local` | `string` | yes |  | Local-language label of the registration unit, as published |
| `unit_kind` | `string` | no |  | Source unit kind, such as district, state or registration_office; plate_policy maps it to a place or state level |
| `scope` | `string` | no |  | Whether the code identifies a registration unit or only associates an entity |
| `series_status` | `string` | no |  | Temporal status of the assertion |
| `series_id` | `string` | yes |  | Source series identifier the assertion belongs to |
| `subdivision_scope` | `string` | yes |  | Narrower context the assertion requires, such as a state series |
| `subdivision_codes` | `list<element: string>` | no |  | ISO 3166-2 identifiers the source gives for the unit; empty when none |
| `source` | `string` | no |  | Configured upstream source name |
| `source_url` | `string` | no |  | URL of the pinned document or query the assertion comes from |
| `license` | `string` | no |  | Licence identifier of that document |

Enumerated columns:

- `scope`
  - `registration_unit`: The source lists the code as issued by this registration unit
  - `entity_association`: Wikidata associates the code with an entity; never used for geography
- `series_status`
  - `current`: The source describes the code as in current use
  - `historic`: The source describes a former series or allocation
  - `unknown`: The source does not establish the status

### `plate_formats`

Plate syntax rules: a full-match regular expression per country and series, with the relaxed form that tolerates separators only where the source shows them, the scripts it uses and its specificity. Each rule is checked against its pinned source document when built; rules whose documents are not pinned are left out.

- Grain: One row per source rule; a country has one row per modeled series and source.
- Primary key: none
- Feeds packs: `plates`

Joins:

- `plate_formats.country_code` → `countries.country_code`: The country or territory issuing the plates

| Column | Type | Nullable | Units | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `country_code` | `string` | no |  | ISO-like two-letter code of the issuing country or territory |
| `series_id` | `string` | no |  | Source series identifier |
| `series_status` | `string` | no |  | Temporal status of the series as the format policy records it: current, or historic (a former series, which needs an explicit series to supply geography) |
| `pattern` | `string` | no |  | Full-match regular expression over the normalized plate text |
| `relaxed_pattern` | `string` | no |  | The pattern with separators optional or varied only at the positions the source shows |
| `code_group` | `string` | yes |  | Name of the capture group holding the registration code; null for series without one |
| `scripts` | `list<element: string>` | no |  | Script names the pattern uses, from plate_policy script_patterns |
| `fixed_national_marks` | `list<element: string>` | no |  | Literal national marks within the serial |
| `specificity_bits` | `double` | no | bits | Information heuristic of the pattern against a 36-character baseline; not a count of valid plates |
| `provenance` | `string` | no |  | JSON source fields of the pinned document: URL, licence, attribution, revision, digest and retrieval time |
| `source` | `string` | no |  | Configured upstream source name |
| `source_file` | `string` | no |  | Pinned file name of the source document |
| `source_url` | `string` | no |  | URL of the pinned source document |
| `license` | `string` | no |  | Licence identifier of that document |

### `plate_policy`

The frozen plate matching and ranking policy (input normalization, code separators, unit-kind levels, script patterns, weights, geographic restrictions and the Unicode decimal digits used for code equality), from config/policies/plate_country/inference.yaml.

- Grain: Exactly one row.
- Primary key: none
- Feeds packs: `plates`

| Column | Type | Nullable | Units | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `policy_json` | `string` | no |  | The policy as one JSON object |

### `plate_priors`

Observed road motor vehicle counts per country, the weak prior that orders candidate countries for a plate without a country. Empty when no vehicle-stock source is pinned; the plates pack then ranks by format evidence alone.

- Grain: One row per country with a published count.
- Primary key: `country_code`
- Feeds packs: `plates`

Joins:

- `plate_priors.country_code` → `countries.country_code`: The counted country or territory

| Column | Type | Nullable | Units | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `country_code` | `string` | no |  | ISO-like two-letter code of the counted country or territory |
| `vehicles` | `uint64` | no | vehicles | Published road motor vehicle count; definitions and dates differ between countries |
| `year` | `int64` | no | calendar year | Year of the published count |
| `source_label` | `string` | no |  | Country label as the source table prints it |
| `source` | `string` | no |  | Configured upstream source name |
| `source_url` | `string` | no |  | URL of the pinned source document |
| `license` | `string` | no |  | Licence identifier of that document |
| `provenance` | `string` | no |  | JSON source fields and the table row the count comes from |

### `postal_codes`

GeoNames postal codes with place names, administrative names and a located point joined to the cell geography. Codes keep their spaces and leading zeros.

- Grain: One row per postal-code observation; a code can repeat for different place names or variants.
- Primary key: `source`, `source_id`
- Feeds packs: `postal`

Joins:

- `postal_codes.country_id` → `places.place_id`: The country place of the cell the point falls in; null when the row is unlocated or unassigned
- `postal_codes.state_id` → `places.place_id`: The first-level subdivision place of that cell; null when none is assigned
- `postal_codes.city_id` → `places.place_id`: The selected settlement of that cell, a canonical city or a standalone rural settlement; null when none is assigned

| Column | Type | Nullable | Units | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | `string` | yes in Arrow; no for the logical key |  | Configured upstream source name |
| `source_id` | `string` | yes in Arrow; no for the logical key |  | Identifier of the original observation within its source |
| `country_code` | `string` | yes |  | Source or reconciled ISO-like two-letter country code |
| `postal_code` | `string` | yes |  | Postal code as text; preserve spaces and leading zeros |
| `place_name` | `string` | yes |  | Source postal place name |
| `admin1_name` | `string` | yes |  | Original level-1 administrative name |
| `admin1_code` | `string` | yes |  | Original level-1 administrative code |
| `admin2_name` | `string` | yes |  | Original level-2 administrative name |
| `admin2_code` | `string` | yes |  | Original level-2 administrative code |
| `admin3_name` | `string` | yes |  | Original level-3 administrative name |
| `admin3_code` | `string` | yes |  | Original level-3 administrative code |
| `accuracy` | `string` | yes |  | Original source positional-accuracy category, not metres |
| `variant` | `string` | yes |  | Original postal observation variant |
| `latitude` | `double` | yes | degrees north | WGS84 latitude; positive north |
| `longitude` | `double` | yes | degrees east | WGS84 longitude; positive east |
| `h3` | `string` | yes |  | Lowercase hexadecimal H3 cell index, without 0x |
| `h3_uint64` | `uint64` | yes |  | Same H3 index as an unsigned 64-bit integer |
| `h3_resolution` | `uint8` | yes | H3 level | Resolution of this stored H3 index |
| `source_release` | `string` | yes |  | Pinned upstream release or inventory identifier |
| `license` | `string` | yes |  | Upstream licence identifier |
| `provenance` | `string` | yes |  | JSON source evidence and transformation provenance |
| `country_id` | `string` | yes |  | Reconciled country place identifier |
| `state_id` | `string` | yes |  | Reconciled first-level subdivision place identifier |
| `city_id` | `string` | yes |  | Selected settlement place ID, including standalone rural settlements; null if unassigned |
| `cell_country_code` | `string` | yes |  | Country code assigned by the geographic cell join |
| `cell_status` | `string` | yes |  | Cell join status: matched, unassigned, ineligible, pending or unlocated |
| `country_disagrees` | `bool` | yes |  | Whether source and cell country codes disagree; null if not comparable |

Enumerated columns:

- `cell_status`
  - `matched`: The point's cell is stored and has a country assignment
  - `unassigned`: The cell is stored but no country is assigned to it
  - `ineligible`: The cell is outside the stored land and near-shore coverage
  - `pending`: No cell data exists for the point's block in this release, so no decision was made
  - `unlocated`: The row has no coordinates, so there is no cell to join

### `subdivisions`

First-level administrative divisions as published by GeoNames admin1 codes, linked to the reconciled subdivision places.

- Grain: One row per GeoNames first-level division code.
- Primary key: `code`
- Feeds packs: `core`, `postal`, `airports`, `locode`, `phone`, `ip`, `plates`

Joins:

- `subdivisions.country_id` → `places.place_id`: The country place named by the row's country code; null when the code matches no place
- `subdivisions.place_id` → `places.place_id`: The single place the row resolves to; null when the link is ambiguous, unmatched or pending

| Column | Type | Nullable | Units | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | `string` | no |  | Configured upstream source name |
| `source_id` | `string` | no |  | Identifier of the original observation within its source |
| `code` | `string` | yes in Arrow; no for the logical key |  | Published entity code |
| `code_system` | `string` | yes |  | Namespace of the published administrative code |
| `country_code` | `string` | yes |  | Source or reconciled ISO-like two-letter country code |
| `name` | `string` | yes |  | Preferred display name |
| `type` | `string` | yes |  | Source-specific entity classification |
| `parent_code` | `string` | yes |  | Original source parent administrative code |
| `geoname_id` | `string` | yes |  | GeoNames identifier represented as text |
| `name_ascii` | `string` | yes |  | Source ASCII name |
| `source_release` | `string` | no |  | Pinned upstream release or inventory identifier |
| `license` | `string` | no |  | Upstream licence identifier |
| `provenance` | `string` | no |  | JSON source evidence and transformation provenance |
| `country_id` | `string` | yes |  | Reconciled country place identifier |
| `place_id` | `string` | yes |  | Uniquely matched reconciled place; null for ambiguous or unmatched observations |
| `link_status` | `string` | yes |  | Identifier link status: matched, ambiguous, unmatched or pending |
| `link_method` | `string` | yes |  | Rule used for the identifier link |
| `place_ids` | `list<element: string>` | yes |  | All candidate place identifiers; ambiguity is preserved |

Enumerated columns:

- `code_system`
  - `GeoNames-admin1`: GeoNames country-dot-admin1 codes such as BE.BRU
- `link_status`
  - `matched`: Exactly one candidate place; place_id is set
  - `ambiguous`: Several candidate places; all are in place_ids and place_id is null
  - `unmatched`: No candidate place was found
  - `pending`: The row refers to a country that is expected in the release but was not reconciled in this build
- `link_method`
  - `source country code`: The row's own country code identifies the country
  - `explicit code or administrative crosswalk`: The published subdivision code maps to a place through the code crosswalk
  - `GeoNames administrative identity`: The row's GeoNames identifier identifies the place
  - `exact country-scoped administrative alias`: The normalized name equals a place alias within the same country
  - `source-qualified administrative alias`: A name qualified by its source administrative context equals a place alias
  - `territory fixed-line prefix language`: Candidate countries were narrowed by the territory's fixed-line numbering pattern
  - `no numbering-pattern support; retained source candidates`: No numbering pattern could narrow the candidates, so every source country is kept

- Primary key: `source`, `source_id`
- Feeds packs: `core`

| `license` | `string` | no |  | Upstream licence identifier |
| `provenance` | `string` | no |  | JSON source evidence and transformation provenance |

| `h3` | `string` | yes |  | Lowercase hexadecimal H3 cell index, without 0x |
| `h3_uint64` | `uint64` | yes |  | Same H3 index as an unsigned 64-bit integer |
